_note: Enterprise search pattern library for the search experiment agent: one search box over first-party (1P) content and third-party (3P) connector content, a typeahead dropdown before Enter, a full results page after Enter, and an answer panel. Families map metric names; at work, metric_families.json in the overlay maps the team's names exactly. Deep dives with 'sql' name a cut template the agent can run; 'needs' and confirms_when / refutes_when let explain.py score the result. A candidate is confirmed only when a cut finds the effect where the mechanism acts AND its control cut (role 'control') shows what the usual look-alikes would not: the effect absent where the mechanism can't act, or present in a group a look-alike can't reach. One agreeing cut alone makes it 'fits a cut'. A control cut with relative_to is read against the reference effect: 'absent' confirms when its interval rules out that share of the reference change; 'present' refutes when it does.

full_page_share._why: the guard counts the full-page share as moved only at 1% or more of itself: a smaller shift in the query mix can't bias a full-page ratio by more than a fraction of that

match: ^full-page queries per user without connected apps
^typeahead resolution of known-item queries, users without connected apps
^1p long-click share, full-page queries with no answer

patterns.name: 3P results take top positions from 1P results
patterns.mechanism: 3P results now hold top positions that 1P results held before. 1P clicks decrease on the queries where 3P clicks increase. Total success changes little.
patterns.source: Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen, KDD 2017 (clicks shift between page elements); zero-sum first page in federated search

deep_dives.cut: 1P long-click share on 3P-eligible queries, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: the 1P loss sits on queries that had a 3P candidate
deep_dives.refutes: 1P long clicks hold on those queries

deep_dives.cut: 1P long-click share on queries with no 3P candidate, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: queries the boost can't touch are unchanged
deep_dives.refutes: they lose 1P clicks too (the cause is elsewhere)

deep_dives.cut: rank of the first 1P long click, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: 1P long clicks move from rank 1 to rank 2
deep_dives.refutes: the rank of the first 1P long click is unchanged

deep_dives.cut: per-tenant concentration of the 1P loss
deep_dives.confirms: the loss spreads across tenants
deep_dives.refutes: one or two large tenants carry it

patterns.owner_question: Are more 3P clicks worth fewer 1P clicks on the same queries?

patterns.name: 3P clicks replace success and do not add to it
patterns.mechanism: The extra 3P clicks occur on queries that already had a success. 3P clicks increase, but success does not.
patterns.source: Hassan et al., CIKM 2013 (clicks are not satisfaction)

deep_dives.cut: any-source success share on 3P-eligible queries, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: success holds (inside its band) where 3P clicks rose
deep_dives.refutes: success rises on those queries

patterns.owner_question: If the extra 3P clicks do not add success, what does the change give users?

patterns.name: Typeahead misses send known-item queries to the full page
patterns.mechanism: Typeahead finds fewer known-item queries, so more of them go to the full results page. Full-page metrics change because the query mix changes, not because the full-page results change.
patterns.source: funnel between surfaces; Kohavi et al., KDD 2012 (metrics that move for the wrong reason)

deep_dives.cut: known-item share of full-page queries, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: more of the full-page queries are known-item queries
deep_dives.refutes: the full-page query mix is unchanged

deep_dives.cut: typeahead resolution of known-item queries for users without connected apps, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: typeahead resolves fewer known-item queries for everyone, not only for users with connected apps
deep_dives.refutes: it holds for users without connected apps (the drop comes from one group's extra queries)

deep_dives.cut: full-page share of all queries, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: a larger share of queries reaches the full page
deep_dives.refutes: the share reaching the full page is unchanged

patterns.owner_question: Typeahead now finds fewer known items. What does the new model give in return?

patterns.name: Answers replace 1P clicks
patterns.mechanism: The answer panel shows on more queries and answers some of them, so users click 1P results less. Success includes answers, so success stays the same or increases.
patterns.source: Li et al., SIGIR 2009 (good abandonment); Chuklin and Serdyukov, SIGIR 2012

deep_dives.cut: share of full-page queries answered without a 1P click, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: more queries end with an answer and no click
deep_dives.refutes: answered-without-click queries are flat

deep_dives.cut: 1P long-click share on full-page queries with no answer shown, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: queries with no answer keep their 1P long clicks
deep_dives.refutes: they lose 1P long clicks too (the cause is elsewhere)

patterns.owner_question: Are answers a good replacement for the 1P clicks that they replace?

patterns.name: Users with connected apps search again and succeed less
patterns.mechanism: Users with connected 3P apps make more full-page queries that end without success. Query volume increases and success decreases. The extra queries also change per-query rates, for example typeahead and 1P click rates.
patterns.source: Hassan et al., WSDM 2013 (struggling searchers); Song et al., WWW 2013

deep_dives.cut: full-page queries per authorized user, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: authorized users search more
deep_dives.refutes: authorized users search as often as before

deep_dives.cut: full-page queries per user without connected apps, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: users without connected apps search as often as before
deep_dives.refutes: they search more too (the cause isn't the connected apps)

patterns.owner_question: Why do users with connected apps search again more? Is the change the cause?

patterns.name: Slower results decrease engagement
patterns.mechanism: The test arm shows results more slowly. Slower pages get fewer clicks and more abandonment, and this can hide a relevance gain. Speed effects usually increase over weeks.

deep_dives.cut: success and 1P long clicks by latency bucket, per arm
deep_dives.confirms: the loss sits in the slow buckets
deep_dives.refutes: the loss is flat across latency buckets

patterns.source: Brutlag, Google, 2009 (400 ms delay: -0.44% searches in weeks 1-3, -0.76% in weeks 4-6, still -0.21% after removal); Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen: Twelve Common Metric Interpretation Pitfalls, KDD 2017 (latency moved by page mix)
patterns.owner_question: Is the latency cost worth the gain of the change?

patterns.name: A ratio changed because its denominator changed
patterns.mechanism: {ratio} changed because {denominator} changed ({denominator_change}), not because {numerator} changed. The change is about volume, not quality.

deep_dives.cut: {numerator} and {denominator} per user, side by side
deep_dives.confirms: the denominator carries the change
deep_dives.refutes: the numerator moves too

deep_dives.cut: what changed the {denominator} (query volume, sessions, logging of searches)
deep_dives.confirms: a volume or logging change explains it
deep_dives.refutes: volume is steady

deep_dives.cut: the same clicks over the finest denominator that doesn't move itself (for example clicks per session)
deep_dives.confirms: the effect disappears on a stable denominator
deep_dives.refutes: the effect holds on a stable denominator

patterns.source: Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen: Twelve Common Metric Interpretation Pitfalls, KDD 2017 (module CTR -40% while clicks +74% and impressions +200%)

patterns.name: The effect is in one segment
patterns.mechanism: Most of the change in {metric} comes from {segment} ({share} of the total change). The segments differ more than noise can explain.

deep_dives.cut: {metric} for {segment} vs the rest, with triggered queries only
deep_dives.confirms: the change is real and confined to {segment}
deep_dives.refutes: the other segments move too once diluted traffic is removed

deep_dives.cut: what the treatment changes for {segment} (ranking features, coverage, rendering)
deep_dives.confirms: a mechanism specific to {segment}
deep_dives.refutes: nothing in the change targets {segment}

deep_dives.cut: sample split and event logging within {segment}, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: the segment is balanced and logs the same way
deep_dives.refutes: the segment itself is imbalanced or logs differently (an artifact)

patterns.source: Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen: Twelve Common Metric Interpretation Pitfalls, KDD 2017 (effects confined to a country, browser or version); tail-query lifts reported for semantic retrieval (snippet-level)

patterns.name: The effect decreases over time
patterns.mechanism: The effect is smaller for each day that users have the treatment, so the long-term effect is probably smaller than the average. A ranking effect that decreases needs a second look.

deep_dives.cut: effect by days since first exposure, per weekly cohort
deep_dives.confirms: every cohort fades the same way
deep_dives.refutes: late cohorts start lower (cohort mix, not novelty)

deep_dives.cut: new vs returning users
deep_dives.confirms: returning users fade
deep_dives.refutes: only new users differ

patterns.source: Song, Shi, Fu, WWW 2013; Brutlag 2009; Hohnhold, O'Brien, Tang, KDD 2015 (ads blindness grows over months)

patterns.name: A data or logging problem, not user behavior
patterns.mechanism: A validity check found a problem in the data. The changes can come from logging, assignment or export problems, not from users.

deep_dives.cut: event counts per user by arm for every logged event the change could touch
deep_dives.confirms: one arm logs differently
deep_dives.refutes: logging is identical

deep_dives.cut: exposure counts by day, platform and browser
deep_dives.confirms: the imbalance sits in one slice
deep_dives.refutes: the imbalance is everywhere (assignment problem)

deep_dives.cut: client-logged vs server-logged versions of the same metric, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: only client events move (telemetry loss differs by arm)
deep_dives.refutes: client and server agree

deep_dives.cut: share of users removed by bot and spam filters, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: filters remove different shares in each arm
deep_dives.refutes: filter rates match

patterns.source: Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen: Twelve Common Metric Interpretation Pitfalls, KDD 2017 (telemetry loss in one arm, bot filters hitting engaged users, metric-level sample ratio mismatch)

_sources: Base kinds (ratio, segment, check) copied from skills/ds-experiment/references/search_patterns.json; enterprise patterns from the Fable enterprise-search review (2026-10-13).
